newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks edge up to another closing high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks edge up to another closing high.

text.p: Swiss shares edged to another closing high as profit taking in Roche was offset by buying in bank shares.
Roche certificates, the market's favourite stock in the past few weeks, slid 145 francs to 11,985. One dealer said a correction following recent speculation-driven highs was normal.
Roche announced on Wednesday it would take over big U.S. flavours firm Tastemaker, disappointing some investors who had hoped for an even larger deal, one trader noted.
Banking groups UBS, SBC and CS Group were underpinned by their decision to set up a Holocaust memorial fund, defusing boycott threats by Jewish groups.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) added 4.2 points, or 0.1 percent, to 4,309.7 points.
It was the sixth record close in a row for the SMI. The day's high was 4,312.5 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 3.30 points, or 0.12 percent, to 2,742.47.
Further development on the Swiss exchange was expected to depend on whether Wall Street would keep its current level.
Novartis was pushed higher after switches from Roche, one trader said. Novartis registered shares soared 18 francs to 1,677.
On Wednesday, Novartis gave details about the imminent spin-off of subsidiary Ciba Specialty Chemicals, which one dealer said may also have been a reason for the firmer bias.

UBS bearers led the actives list, gaining 18 francs, or 1.48 francs, to 1,237. Traders also cited a recommendation by Merrill Lych as reason for the advance. CS Group and SBC firmed 0.75 francs to 148.50 and 1.50 francs to 275.50, respectively. Insurers were generally slightly weaker.
Nestle lost six francs to 1,552. Surveillance gave up 60 francs to 3,250.
ABB and Alusuisse slid 0.7 percent each to 1,809 and 1,191 francs, respectively. Sulzer added 14 francs to 954.
